Q: How do I get my aim cursor to stay near the border of the circle? A:

I have not used Unity 3d, but I have done lots of geometry math in both 2D and 3D.

I would try my best to avoid conversion to or from angles, and especially try to avoid euler angles as much as possible. I'm not sure exactly what you are trying to do, but if you need to create a rotation from a direction there are probably better ways. In most cases it is possible to use vector math to do things, but it does require you to be fairly familiar with your linear algebra.

From your description it sounds like you just need to normalize your direction, that will keep its direction. You can then multiply it with whatever length you want your vector to have.

Just keep in mind to check for directions that have a length close to zero, otherwise you will get an invalid vector when you try to normalize.

Q: Why can't I initialize vector<foo> from std::initializer_list<string> if foo has a non-explicit constructor from string? A:

Just because A is convertible to B doesn't mean initializer_list<A> is convertible to initializer_list<B>. The latter two are completely unrelated types.

As to the fix, just use the range constructor.

std::vector<testNetInfo> netInfo(initList.begin(), initList.end());

Q: PyTorch training issue with EfficientNetB3 | Validation Accuracy plateu A:

It would be helpful to see the loss curves of both training loss and validation loss, or, likewise, the corresponding accuracy curves. Two things that I would look out for there:

  • Do both training and validation loss or accuracy plateau at a less then ideal value? Then maybe the learning rate is too high or the model is too small.
  • Does the validation loss or accuracy start plateauing (or maybe starts increasing (loss) / decreasing (accuracy) again) while the training loss continues to decrease / training accuracy continues to increase? This would imply overfitting, and perhaps more aggressive augmentations and dropout can help.

Q: Constructing a vector of object using std::initializer_list A:

You attempt to create a vector of Cols from an initializer list of std::strings. There's no conversion from std::initializer_list<std::string> to a std::initializer_list<Col> even though there is a conversion from std::string to Col. Thats the reason using the iterator constructor works (conversion from std::string to Col) but not the one taking the initializer list.

Generally speaking, there is no implicit relation between X<T> and X<U> other than being instantiations of X. For example there is also no direct conversion from std::vector<std::string> to std::vector<Col> (while you can construct a std::vector<Col> with iterators to the vector of strings).

Q: ECS Task in private subnet is not able to pull image from ECR, using AWS PrivateLink A:

Your idea of creating a private service, with the usage of endpoints to communicate with AWS Services is nice. But the template is misconfigured. Your private subnet, where the ECS Service is placed, has no route table associated with it, and is needed to routed through a NAT Gateway or associated with appropriate vpc endpoints. You also don't need so many ALB/ECS security groups, it only makes architecture complex and hard to interpret. Your ECS typical network path is ALB (port 80) --> Target group ( HTTP traffic --> port 3000). So it's one ALB SG for public HTTP ingress, and one ECS task SG that only allows port 3000 from the ALB SG, is sufficient. You can allow all outbound or required port ranges.

If you want a more polished version of your design with NAT Gateway, you can find it in this gist : cloudformation_template_gist
